Name: Sarah Apple
Badge: Teacher as Researcher | Sustaining Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

All of these strategies just really encouraged me to slow down and approach our work more thoughtfully. Now I did this in an elective class where we have more time and it was wonderful to slow down and be more intentional with our thinking and our learning. Some of the strategies will also be useful even in a core class that has much swifter pacing. Go slow to go fast? Is that the expression? Sometimes slowing down and doing the thing with more intention and connection will help the students learn and develop the skills faster than the break neck pace at which we are usually forced to learn.

Think back to a moment during the lesson sequence that stands out. It could be a comment from a student, an unexpected challenge or success, a shift in engagement, or a moment when your own thinking changed. Describe what happened and why this moment feels meaningful to you now. What does it reveal:
I think I was mostly struck by their willingness to just dive into this process. They were really hooked by the topic of tech and its impact on their bodies and minds. I did have one student crash out at the multiple articles but she crashes out frequently about a lot of things. Ha. Overall the kids did a great job of following instructions and interacting with the materials - a higher rate of participation than usual. I think that was in part to how I set up the slides with timers and kept us all in unison. So there was pressure to be moving things a long.
As you look over the drafts your students produced in this lesson sequence, what early patterns, surprises, or questions are emerging for you? What aspects of your students’ writing are you most curious to explore more deeply with colleagues during our April regroup? What, if any, questions do you h:
I was curious to see how much they would write since I didn't specify. Most wrote about the same amount. I did have one student very excited that he wrote a lengthy response! Anytime a student is proud of their hard work, it's a win! I have not yet used the UST tool with these pieces so I am looking forward to that process.
